Melissa Anne Hortman (née Haluptzok; May 27, 1970 – June 14, 2025) was an American politician and lawyer who served as the 61st speaker of the Minnesota House of Representatives.
A member of the Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party, she represented northern parts of the Twin Cities metropolitan area in the Minnesota House of Representatives from 2005 to 2025, serving as the House minority leader from 2017 to 2019 and as speaker from 2019 to January 2025.
During her tenure, she advocated for transportation, environmental rights, abortion rights, police reform, and gun control policies.
She was also the chief author of the state's solar energy standard.
On June 14, 2025, Hortman and her husband were assassinated in a politically motivated attack at their home in Brooklyn Park, Minnesota.[1]
Early life and education
[edit]
Hortman was born Melissa Anne Haluptzok in Fridley, Minnesota, on May 27, 1970.[2] She grew up in Spring Lake Park and Andover, and became interested in being a politician at age ten, while watching coverage of the 1980 presidential election.[3] She graduated from Blaine High School in Blaine, Minnesota, in 1988.[4]
Hortman received a Bachelor of Arts (magna cum laude) with a major in philosophy and political science from Boston University in 1991, a Juris Doctor (cum laude) from the University of Minnesota Law School in 1995, and a Master in Public Administration from Harvard Kennedy School in 2018.[5][6]

Vance Boelter, 57, of Green Isle, Minnesota, has been charged by federal complaint with stalking and murdering Minnesota House of Representatives Speaker Emerita Melissa Hortman and her husband, in addition to stalking and shooting Minnesota State Senator John Hoffman and his wife.
According to court documents, in the early morning hours of June 14, 2025, Vance Luther Boelter put into effect a calculated plan to inflict fear and violence upon Minnesota elected officials and their families.
Boelter equipped himself with firearms and body armor, disguised himself as a law enforcement officer, and drove to the home of Senator Hoffman.
Boelter knocked on the door repeatedly, claiming to be a police officer.

Next, Boelter drove to the home of Speaker Emerita and Representative Melissa Hortman.
Meanwhile, local law enforcement, having heard of the shooting at the Hoffman residence, drove to the Hortman household to conduct a safety check.
Upon arriving, officers saw Boelter’s car, a black Ford Explorer SUV designed to look like a law enforcement vehicle.

Since the United States Congress was established with the 1st Congress in 1789, fourteen of its members have been killed while in office, and eighteen have suffered serious injuries from attacks.
The members of Congress were either injured or killed by someone intending serious harm, or there is speculation of lethal intent by an unknown assailant (such as the two congressmen who died of the National Hotel disease).
The first member of Congress to be killed or wounded in office was Henry Wharton Conway who was killed in a duel in 1827.

The most recent member of Congress to be injured was Maxwell Frost who was assaulted in 2026.
All of the 14 members of Congress killed in office were male and 10 were Democrats, three were Republicans, and one was a Democratic-Republican.

Two were women, and three were senators.
Five of those injured were wounded during the 1954 United States Capitol shooting incident.

Keith Self says he was never in any real danger from an alleged assassination plot involving a 17-year-old boy from his hometown of McKinney.

Capitol Police notified him of the threat, federal authorities had already arrested the teenager, Self said.
"When we knew about it, they had him," Self, R-McKinney, told CBS News Texas.
"...
It's more routine than you would think with members of Congress."
Self said he did not know the wording of the threat or how or where it was made.
He said law enforcement informed him that the McKinney teenager had planned to make waves, "perhaps try to shoot at me," and carry out a terrorist attack.
He said it was unclear exactly what that meant.
"The FBI, through the Capitol Police, only tells us so much," Self said.
Self said he did not know how the FBI uncovered the alleged assassination plot, but believed authorities had been aware of the teenager before his arrest.
"I understand that they've known about this kid for a while," he said.
Self declined to speculate about what motivated the alleged plot but said the teenager was "somehow under the influence of the things that we see happening in Texas and certainly in McKinney."
"It's a very unsettled time," Self said.
"We see it, we feel it."
Self said he had received threats before, "but not to this degree and not any that action was taken by law enforcement."
Still, he said he was not fazed by the threat.
"I was in the military for 25 years, deployed multiple times," he said.
"I also knew that the law enforcement had him under control.
Now, it would have been a little different if they had said, 'There's an unknown threat out there.'"
Meanwhile, Self said he was "very grateful" to the FBI for acting before the alleged threat could be carried out.
"So often we hear that somebody does something and then you find out later that the FBI had him on some sort of watch list and didn't take action," Self said.
"So I am very grateful that the FBI took action in this case."
Efforts to reach the FBI and Capitol Police for comment have been unsuccessful.
CBS News Texas will provide updates as more information becomes available.

Democrats hold 9-point edge on midterm congressional ballot
Washington, D.C., October 26, 2026 – An Ipsos analysis of the October Reuters/Ipsos Core Political survey conducted October 22-26 finds that the Democratic Party holds a 9-point edge over the Republican Party among likely voters on the 2026 generic congressional ballot.
Overall, 53% of likely voters say they would vote for or lean to the Democratic candidate in their district, compared with 44% who say they would vote for or lean to the Republican candidate.
The election comes amid building public frustration with the Trump administration on economic issues.
Among all Americans, just 25% approve of how President Donald Trump is handling the U.S.
economy, while only 20% approve of his handling of the cost of living.
The president's overall approval rating remains at a near low for his presidency, with just 32% saying they approve.
As ratings of the administration have soured, the Democratic Party has gained ground as the party seen as better able to handle the U.S.
economy (34% prefer the Democratic Party, 28% the Republican Party).
This Democratic advantage is a shift from historical patterns and represents a major change in public assessments since January 2025, when the GOP led on the economy by 17 points.
In recent months, signs of softening support for the president have become visible within the Republican base.
In the current survey, 62% of Republicans approve of the president’s handling of the economy, and just 48% approve of his handling of the cost of living.
Republicans are now more likely to say they approve of his job performance “somewhat” (42%) rather than “strongly” (34%) – a change from the start of Trump's second term.
As has been the case throughout the fall, Democrats continue to express more strong enthusiasm than Republicans toward voting in this fall's midterm elections.

MILWAUKEE — A new Marquette Law School Poll of Wisconsin finds that, in the race for governor, Democrat David Crowley is supported by 49% of likely voters and Republican Tom Tiffany is supported by 46%, with 5% undecided.
Among all registered voters, Crowley is the choice of 46%, and Tiffany is supported by 45%, with 9% undecided.
In August, Crowley had 49% and Tiffany 44% among likely voters, and the race was tied with 44% each among registered voters.
Partisans are strongly behind their nominees, with 95% of Republicans backing Tiffany and 96% of Democrats for Crowley among likely voters.
Independents strongly favor Crowley, with 44% supporting him and 18% supporting Tiffany, but a large 38% are undecided.
Results among registered voters are similar, with a few more voters undecided.
Compared to August, Republican support for Tiffany increased by 4 percentage points, while Democratic support for Crowley slipped by 2 points.
Independent support for Crowley fell by 11 points.
The percentage of independents voting for Tiffany rose by 2 points, while the percentage of independents who are undecided rose by 8 points.
All these figures are among likely voters.
These results are shown in Table 1.
(All results in the tables are stated as percentages.)
Table 1: Vote for governor, by party identification

The final fundraising reports in the race for governor show Democratic billionaires are helping give Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley a late fundraising edge over Republican U.S.
Rep.
Tom Tiffany and the GOP billionaires backing him.
The latest numbers stand out because Tiffany had previously outraised Crowley nearly 2-1 throughout the campaign.
Filings with the Wisconsin Ethics Commission show Crowley raked in around $15.5 million between July 1 and Oct.
19, while Tiffany raised around $10 million.
The lion’s share of the money going to campaigns came by way of transfers from state parties, which face no limits on how much they can accept from wealthy donors or how much they can give to candidates.
Crowley received $11.4 million in transfers during the reporting period from the Democratic Party of Wisconsin, which reported getting $5.5 million from LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman; $2 million from former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg; $1.5 million from philanthropist Lynn Schusterman; and $1 million each from philanthropists Nina Singh Wanstrath and Lynde Uihlein.
Tiffany reported around $9 million in transfers from the Republican Party of Wisconsin, which got a single $13 million donation from GOP megadonor Diane Hendricks.
In the latest reporting period, Hendricks was one of just six donors to the state Republican Party, accounting for nearly all of the party’s fundraising haul from individual donors.

Before the uptick for Democrats in the latest report, Tiffany had dominated Crowley in fundraising in 2026.

Tiffany spent about $47 million over the course of the calendar year compared to about $23 million for Crowley.
The Democratic and Republican parties had seen similar gaps.
The state GOP reported bringing in more than $57 million throughout 2026.
That’s more than twice state Democrats’ haul of around $28 million.
That gap narrowed in the latest finance reports, which showed both parties raised around $15 million since July 1 when all transfers were factored in.
All told this year, Hendricks has donated more than $23 million to the Republican Party, and fellow conservative billionaires Richard and Elizabeth Uihlein have contributed a total of more than $32 million.
Hoffman has been the state Democratic Party’s biggest donor in 2026, giving more than $8.75 million.
In addition to the recent donations from Bloomberg, Schusterman, Wanstrath and Lynde Uihlein, Democratic Illinois Gov.
JB Pritzker gave $1 million to the Democratic Party of Wisconsin shortly after Crowley won the primary.

Réunie le dimanche 25 octobre, la Coordination des Gilets Jaunes appelle à un acte III partout en France le samedi 31 octobre.
Elle appelle ensuite à soutenir la grève du jeudi 5 novembre et à la prolonger par deux journées de blocages et de mobilisations, les vendredi 6 et samedi 7 novembre.
Acte III, le 31 octobre, pour nos libertés
Le président Emmanuel Macron et son gouvernement ont décidé de franchir une étape de plus dans la dérive autoritaire.
Ils interdisent nos manifestations, ferment les centres-villes aux manifestants et imposent des couvre-feux à Marseille, à Lyon, à Paris et à Perpignan.
Pour Emmanuel Macron, seules les organisations syndicales seraient légitimes pour manifester.
Le ministre de la Justice demande aux procureurs de requérir contre des manifestants la privation du droit de vote, le bannissement des réseaux sociaux, et jusqu'à la dénonciation à leur employeur.
Ces décisions vont contre notre Constitution, qui garantit la liberté d'expression et la liberté de manifester.
La répression atteint déjà un niveau record.
En quelques semaines, plus de 10 000 personnes ont été placées en garde à vue, en majorité des mineurs : autant qu'en une année entière de mouvement des gilets jaunes.
Deux personnes sont mortes à Paris en marge des manifestations.
Des adolescents ont été mutilés : à Saint-Étienne et à Lens, deux jeunes de 17 et 15 ans ont eu la main arrachée ; à Mulhouse et à Tours, deux jeunes de 17 et 16 ans ont perdu un œil.
À Strasbourg, à Clermont-Ferrand, à Bordeaux et à Montpellier, des manifestants ont été gravement blessés au visage et aux yeux.
Nous exigeons la levée immédiate de tous les couvre-feux, l'amnistie des manifestantes et des manifestants arrêtés, et des enquêtes sur l'intégralité des violences commises par les forces dites de l'ordre, jusqu'au plus haut niveau de la chaîne de commandement.
Pour l'acte III, nous invitons à tenir de grands rassemblements en sit-in, au point de départ ou d'arrivée des cortèges, avant ou après les manifestations, et devant les mairies là où il n'y a pas de cortège.
Nous invitons à y donner la parole aux travailleuses et aux travailleurs en lutte, à la jeunesse mobilisée et à tous les collectifs engagés dans le mouvement.
En prélude, le vendredi 30 octobre, nous appelons à un rassemblement casserolade devant l'Assemblée nationale de 18 h à 21 h, et à des casserolades partout en France le même soir.
Des assemblées de convergence partout en France
Depuis le 17 octobre, des assemblées de convergence se sont tenues dans de nombreuses villes.
Selon les lieux, elles s'appellent assemblées inter-luttes, inter-orgas, citoyennes ou assemblées du peuple, et les assemblées interprofessionnelles déjà existantes les ont rejointes.
L'acte III renforcera ces assemblées, interprofessionnelles, interfacs ou du mouvement climat, et en fera naître là où il n'y en a pas encore.
Partout, elles doivent associer les travailleuses et les travailleurs, les jeunesses, les quartiers populaires et l'outre-mer.
Nous appelons à une assemblée nationale des assemblées de convergence, dans la seconde quinzaine de novembre.
La ville d'accueil sera annoncée prochainement.
Dans chaque assemblée locale, puis nationalement, nous construirons les revendications de tous les secteurs mobilisés.
Elles serviront de base à des états généraux.
Si le gouvernement ne répond pas à l'ensemble de ces revendications, Emmanuel Macron et son gouvernement devront partir.
Au-delà des exigences de l'urgence, nous voulons construire une nouvelle société.
Nous reprendrons l'ensemble des travaux des Gilets jaunes et de nombreux autres collectifs pour lancer un processus constituant, pour un pouvoir du peuple, par le peuple, pour le peuple, et la fin du régime de monarchie présidentielle.
Le 5 novembre du peuple, puis l'acte IV
Le jeudi 5 novembre, nous appelons à soutenir la grève générale interprofessionnelle appelée par l'intersyndicale, et les blocages de lycées et de facs partout en France.
Les vendredi 6 et samedi 7 novembre, nous appelons à reconduire et à généraliser la grève, pour l'égalité réelle : blocages et mobilisations dans toute la France, puis le samedi 7 novembre, acte IV, avec de grandes manifestations partout en France.
Avec la jeunesse, contre le racisme
Nous appelons à venir en nombre soutenir tous les rassemblements antiracistes et les hommages aux victimes de la police et de l'extrême droite.
Nous appelons aussi à soutenir les mobilisations lycéennes, qui reprendront dès la rentrée du lundi 2 novembre, avec deux premiers temps forts : le mardi 3 et le jeudi 5 novembre.
Le 31 octobre pour nos libertés, du 5 au 7 novembre pour l'égalité réelle.
Le peuple uni ne sera jamais vaincu !

Du côté de Tours, ça sera place Jean-Jaurès, à 14 h, et à Toulouse, au métro Jean-Jaurès, à la même heure.
Pour les sit-in, il y en aura un peu partout, dans chaque métropole et petite ville aussi, c’est le cas par exemple à Avranches (50), Saint-Quentin (02), Aurillac (15) ou encore à Rochefort (17).

Des ronds-points bloqués ?
Alors que les blocages de ronds-points étaient au cœur des manifestations des Gilets jaunes en 2019, samedi dernier, certains blocages ont eu lieu, mais nous restons très loin des records d’il y a sept ans.
Samedi 24 octobre, environ 60 blocages de ronds-points étaient prévus dans toute la France et 13 à l’abord des péages.
Cette fois-ci pour cet acte III, la coordination prévoit pour l’instant le blocage de seulement 6 ronds-points et 2 stations-service, notamment celle de Finhan, dans le 82, à partir de 10 h.
Pour rappel, comme évoqué dans cet article d’actu.fr, bloquer une station-service peut tomber sous le coup de la loi.
Un tribunal peut notamment retenir le délit d’entrave à la circulation en application du Code de la route, ou le délit d’entrave à la liberté du travail prévu par le Code pénal.

General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, 28 October, Member States will vote for the 34th time on a resolution calling for it to end.
Every year at around this time, the assembly – where each of the UN’s 193 Member States has one vote – takes up the “necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba”.
And every year, whatever the political climate, the issue generates plenty of diplomatic heat.
The debate usually spills over two days as countries and regional groups take the floor to explain their positions.
A 33-vote record
The assembly has called for an end to the embargo, first imposed in 1960, on 33 previous occasions.
Support has grown markedly since the first vote in 1992, when 59 countries backed the resolution, three opposed it, 71 abstained and 46 did not vote.
It peaked at 191 votes in favour in 2015, 2016 and 2017, during the thaw in relations under US President Barack Obama.
The United States and Israel voted against in 2015 and 2017; in 2016, both abstained.
Some countries have shifted position as governments have changed, but many have held the same line for decades.
Canada, China and Russia have long voted in favour, while the United States, backed by Israel, has voted against every year bar one.
A tightening squeeze
This year’s debate comes as the Trump administration has tightened the embargo – a move that has led to an energy crisis and possible humanitarian collapse, according to the UN Resident Coordinator in Cuba, Francisco Pichon.
The World Health Organization (WHO) has also warned that energy shortages are taking a toll on health.
In May, senior UN officials reported that more than 100,000 surgical procedures had been postponed.
Cuban authorities have repeatedly pointed to further damage to the health system, including delays to vaccination programmes and patients with chronic illnesses unable to get a stable supply of medicines.
This year, President Donald Trump has also raised the possibility of military intervention in Cuba.
Successive UN High Commissioners for Human Rights and independent UN experts have condemned the embargo and other unilateral US sanctions, warning that they threaten Cubans’ rights to health, life, food and development.
Tensions spill over
Those tensions were on display in the chamber on Tuesday when Cuba’s Foreign Minister, Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla, interrupted the US Ambassador, Mike Waltz, on a point of order midway through his statement.
The exchange escalated into a heated row between the two, prompting the President of the General Assembly to briefly suspend the session.
The debate later resumed without further incident.
Mr.
Waltz rejected the premise of the debate, arguing that Cuba’s crisis was the fault of its own government, not the embargo.
“There is no blockade,” he said.
If there were, he argued, there would be no explaining US exports to Cuba – which he put at more than $876 million in the first eight months of 2026 – or shipments from Canada, Spain, Mexico, China, Russia, the European Union and UN agencies.
The country’s wealth had not vanished, he said, but had “simply” passed from ordinary Cubans into the hands of the ruling elite.
Mr.
Rodríguez is due to deliver his statement on Wednesday.

Де насправді перебувають російські війська
16 жовтня начальник Генштабу Росії Валерій Герасимов під час доповіді Володимиру Путіну заявив про нібито захоплення Добропілля, Олексієво-Дружківки та Сергіївки.
Також він стверджував, що російські війська "перебувають" за п'ять кілометрів від Запоріжжя.
"Телеграф" зібрав актуальні дані карти DeepState станом на 16 жовтня, щоб перевірити, де розташовані позиції противника.
Про доповідь начальника Генштабу РФ повідомили росЗМІ.
За словами Герасимова, Добропілля нібито перейшло під контроль угруповання військ "Центр", а Олексієво-Дружківку зайняли підрозділи угруповання "Юг".
Де перебувають російські війська
За даними карти DeepState станом на 16 жовтня, відстані до найближчих позицій противника становлять:
- Добропілля, Донецька область — близько 3,4 км.
- Олексієво-Дружківка, Донецька область — близько 4 км.
- Сергіївка, Донецька область — близько 4,89 км.
- Запоріжжя — близько 21 км.
Що відбувається на фронті
За даними Генштабу ЗСУ за 16 жовтня, упродовж минулої доби на Покровському напрямку російські війська здійснили 60 атак.
Противник намагався просунутися, зокрема, у районах Добропілля та Сергіївки.
Моніторингові канали також повідомляють, що російські підрозділи намагаються використовувати погіршення погодних умов і ранкові тумани для штурмів.
Зокрема, на Добропільському напрямку противник регулярно відправляє малі групи на мотоциклах у бік міста, намагаючись прорватися до забудови та закріпитися.
Такі спроби не завжди завершуються успіхом: російські військові втрачають транспорт і потрапляють під удари українських безпілотників.
Як пише Агентство.Новости, за даними Conflict Intelligence Team (CIT), російські військові присутні на південних околицях Добропілля та на схід від нього, однак стабільність їхньої присутності залишається незрозумілою.
OSINT-аналітик Кирило Михайлов зазначає, що російські підрозділи намагаються вийти на підступи до Добропілля та періодично проник

logy follows the IOSCO Principles for financial benchmarks: arm’s-length executed transactions only, defined eligibility criteria, outlier handling, and documented procedures.
Moving the index would require committing capital in real transactions at market prices, and contributed data is screened for wash trades and self-dealing.
Settled prints are final by construction: each period is computed once, after its inputs have closed.
If a confirmed data error is identified, the affected prints are corrected and the correction is noted, but history is never silently restated and methodology changes are not applied retroactively.
Earlier prints drew on fewer contributing sources, and smaller samples produce noisier averages.
As the provider network has grown, print-to-print noise has fallen.
The underlying market itself is also genuinely volatile: unsold compute hours expire worthless, which creates real price movement when demand shifts.
A family of transaction-based indices tracking clearing prices for rented GPU compute in USD per GPU-hour.
It uses anonymized executed trades from a diversified set of independent operators.
No offers or indicative quotes are included.
H100 SXM, H200, A100 SXM4, B200, and RTX PRO 6000 WS.

The platform’s headline number and Price History chart use the daily reference print, defined as the volume-weighted winsorized mean over the 24-hour window ending 4:00 PM ET.
Hourly prints and the 24-hour rolling average are available through the API on Full (sk_live_).
A Premium key is daily-grain only.
H100 history runs from January 2025 at hourly granularity, with sparser data back to mid-2024.
Newer SKUs begin when their volume crossed eligibility, for example B200 from November 2025.
Earlier, sparser history can be shared on request for diligence and backtesting.
Contact the team
A rate card is one provider’s posted price for its own capacity.
The index is a market-wide settlement built from executed trades across many providers, regions, and contract tenors, and it is the same number every counterparty sees.
The index measures the executed on-demand market: the marginal clearing price of compute.
Long-dated reserved contracts trade at negotiated levels around that benchmark, the same way term power or freight contracts trade around spot indices.
That is precisely what makes the index useful as a mark for such contracts, and region- and tenor-tagged data supports basis analysis.

quotes: Each index is computed as the volume-weighted winsorized mean of executed transaction prices for a given GPU type over a rolling one-hour window.

Index values are published as promptly as practicable following the close of each one-hour window, with the reference timestamp corresponding to the window close.
Values are calculated and delivered to the nearest tenth of a cent ($0.001).

As a general matter, Ornn does not restate historical index values.
An exception applies where an error is attributable to data falsification by a contributing provider, or to a calculation error that Ornn determines to be material to benchmark integrity.

At re-verification, machines that no longer satisfy the criteria are suspended pending restoration of compliance.
Suspension is not retroactive: previously published index values are not restated solely because hardware degradation is discovered at re-verification, unless independent evidence indicates that the degradation constituted intentional misrepresentation.
Intentional submission of false, misleading, or manipulated data is treated as a separate and more serious category of non-compliance.
Where reasonable grounds exist, consequences include immediate suspension pending investigation, review of affected historical index values covering the period of the manipulation, restatement where warranted and practicable, and permanent exclusion from the contributor network upon confirmation.
Ornn reserves the right to refer confirmed cases to regulatory and law enforcement authorities.
3.
Index Calculation
3.1 Overview
Each index is computed as the volume-weighted winsorized mean of executed transaction prices for a given GPU type over a rolling one-hour window.
Winsorization retains all observed trades and adjusts only those prices falling outside a defined percentile range, replacing outliers with the corresponding bound values.
Because trade volume is retained at the boundaries, the estimator is resistant to small-sample distortion while preserving the full informational content of every executed transaction.
OCPI applies no smoothing, averaging across windows, or other filtering beyond the winsorization described in this section; each published value reflects only the executed transactions in its own calculation window.

3.7 Publication
Index values are published as promptly as practicable following the close of each one-hour window, with the reference timestamp corresponding to the window close.
Values are calculated and delivered to the nearest tenth of a cent ($0.001).

4.
Index Properties
4.1 Robustness
Beyond the pre-processing controls described in Section 2.1, OCPI benchmarks are calculated in a manner that expresses liquidity sensitivity, further enhancing robustness against distortion.
The volume-weighted winsorized mean provides two complementary layers of protection.
First, volume weighting ensures that a party seeking to shift the index must command sufficient traded volume to alter the weighted mean; this raises the cost of manipulation materially, as influence over the published value is proportional to genuine economic participation in the market.
Second, winsorization caps the influence of extreme prints without discarding trades: every transaction contributes to the calculation, but prices falling outside the eligible range are adjusted to the nearest bound rather than removed.
The winsorizing bounds are themselves robust statistics, drawn from the volume-weighted empirical distribution of the calculation window.
As a result, a coordinated series of off-market prints has limited effect on the published value unless the manipulator commands sufficient traded volume to displace the corresponding fraction of total window volume.
This architecture makes concentrated manipulation materially costly.
4.2 Validation and Restatement
Prior to publication, each index value undergoes internal validation designed to identify anomalous or potentially erroneous values.
Values that deviate materially from recent historical distributions are flagged for review before release.
If a published value is subsequently determined to contain a material error, Ornn publishes a corrected value and notifies affected stakeholders through appropriate channels.
As a general matter, Ornn does not restate historical index values.
An exception applies where an error is attributable to data falsification by a contributing provider, or to a calculation error that Ornn determines to be material to benchmark integrity.
Users relying on OCPI values for settlement purposes are advised to maintain independent records of published values.
4.3 Market Disruption Events
A Market Disruption Event (“MDE”) occurs when Ornn determines that the transaction data available for a calculation window is insufficient to support a reliable index determination.

- Carry-forward.
The most recently published index value is carried forward as the index value for the affected window.
Carry-forward may be applied for a limited number of consecutive calculation windows.
- Suspension.
If carry-forward would be inconsistent with the integrity of the index, or if the carry-forward limit is reached without resolution of the disruption, publication is suspended for the affected windows until the disruption is resolved.

On-demand, pay-as-you-go rentals rather than reserved or committed contracts.
On-demand prices clear continuously and move with real-time supply and demand, which makes them the cleanest available signal of current AI compute usage.
Reserved and long-term contracts are negotiated around that on-demand benchmark, the same way term contracts in other commodities trade around a spot reference.
On the order of 150 providers contribute to each index and roughly a thousand transactions are observed per day, with the majority of volume in the United States.
Coverage grows as new providers are verified and integrated.
All eligible trades pool into one global, volume-weighted distribution, so a region’s influence on the print is its share of executed volume.
Every trade stays tagged with its region, GPU type, and quantity, which means regional cuts such as US-only series can be produced, and regional basis shows up as dispersion around the global print.
If no eligible volume prints in a window, the index holds the last published value rather than interpolating.
Because inputs are pooled globally across many providers, fully empty windows are rare and become rarer as coverage grows.
The methodology follows the IOSCO Principles for financial benchmarks: arm’s-length executed transactions only, defined eligibility criteria, outlier handling, and documented procedures.
Moving the index would require committing capital in real transactions at market prices, and contributed data is screened for wash trades and self-dealing.
Settled prints are final by construction: each period is computed once, after its inputs have closed.
If a confirmed data error is identified, the affected prints are corrected and the correction is noted, but history is never silently restated and methodology changes are not applied retroactively.
Earlier prints drew on fewer contributing sources, and smaller samples produce noisier averages.
As the provider network has grown, print-to-print noise has fallen.
The underlying market itself is also genuinely volatile: unsold compute hours expire worthless, which creates real price movement when demand shifts.

Every endpoint here works without a key or an account.
Anonymous requests are rate-limited per IP.

- Compute (OCPI): current price, plus 3 months of daily history, for 5 GPUs.
- Tokens (OTPI): 1 month of daily settled prices, for 4 labs.
With a key
Full history, every tracked GPU and lab, plus memory prices, datacenter sites and LLM coding analytics.
Get a key at data.ornn.com; full reference at data.ornn.com/docs.

GPU identifiers, for use as gpuName.

curl "https://api.ornnai.com/api/gpu-types"
curl "https://api.ornnai.com/api/gpu-types-free"

Using humans to generate questions also presents limitations.
Human participants might not ask diverse questions, may favor certain topics that do not probe a model’s general capabilities, or may construct their prompts poorly (Zheng et al., 2024).
In this work, we introduce a framework for benchmarking LLMs designed to minimize both test set contamination and the pitfalls of LLM judging and human crowdsourcing.
We use this framework to create LiveBench, the first benchmark with these three desiderata: (1) LiveBench contains frequently-updated questions based on recent information sources; (2) LiveBench is scored automatically according to the objective ground truth without the use of an LLM judge; and (3) LiveBench questions are drawn from a diverse set of six categories.
We ensure (2) by only including questions that have an objectively correct answer.
LiveBench questions are difficult: no current model achieves higher than 70% accuracy.
Questions are added and updated on a monthly basis, and we release new tasks and harder versions of tasks over time so that LiveBench can distinguish among the capabilities of LLMs as they improve in the future.
Overview of tasks.
LiveBench currently consists of 18 tasks across 6 categories: math, coding, reasoning, language, instruction following, and data analysis.
Each task falls into one of two types: (1) tasks which use an information source for their questions, e.g., data analysis questions based on recent Kaggle datasets, or fixing typos in recent arXiv abstracts; and (2) tasks which are more challenging or diverse versions of existing benchmark tasks, e.g., from Big-Bench Hard (Suzgun et al., 2023) or IFEval (Zhou et al., 2023a).
The categories and tasks included in LiveBench are:
- •
Math: modified questions based on high school math competitions from the past 11 months, as well as harder versions of AMPS questions (Hendrycks et al., 2021)
- •
Coding: code generation questions from recent Leetcode and AtCoder questions (via LiveCodeBench (Jain et al., 2024)), as well as a novel code completion task
- •
Reasoning: a harder version of Web of Lies from Big-Bench Hard (Suzgun et al., 2023), and novel Zebra Puzzles (e.g., (Jeremy, 2009)) and spatial reasoning questions
- •
Language Comprehension: Connections word puzzles, a typo-fixing task, and a movie synopsis unscrambling task for recent movies on IMDb and Wikipedia
- •
Instruction Following: four tasks to paraphrase, simplify, summarize, or generate stories about recent new articles from The Guardian (Guardian Media Group, 1821), subject to one or more instructions such as word limits or incorporating specific elements in the response
- •
Data Analysis: three tasks using recent datasets from Kaggle and Socrata, specifically, table reformatting (among JSON, JSONL, Markdown, CSV, TSV, and HTML), predicting which columns can be used to join two tables, and predicting the correct column type annotation
We evaluate dozens of models, including proprietary models as well as open-source models with sizes ranging from 0.5B to 8x22B.
We release all questions, code, and model answers, and we welcome community engageme

For each model, we compute the score on each task as the average of all questions, we compute the score on each of the six categories as the average of all their tasks, and we compute the final LiveBench score as the average of all six categories.
In Appendix B, we give additional documentation including average input/output tokens and cost to run LiveBench for each API model.
3.1 Discussion of Results
We compare all 40 models on LiveBench according to the experimental setup described above; see Table 1 and Table 2.
We find that o1-preview-2024-09-12 performs the best overall, 6% better than all other models.
o1-preview-2024-09-12 substantially outperforms all other models in the data analysis, language, and math categories.
The next-best model is claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620, which far outperforms all other models in the coding category (although o1-mini outperforms claude-3.5 in code generation, claude-3.5 has the edge in code completion).
o1-mini-2024-09-12 is third overall and is significantly better than all other models in the reasoning category.
The best-performing open-source models are llama-3.1-405b-instruct and qwen2.5-72b-instruct, which virtually tie with each other and outperform gpt-4-turbo.
The best-performing small open-source model is phi-3.5-moe-instruct (see Table 2): with only 6.6B active parameters, it outperforms gpt-3.5 and is on par with mixtral-8x22b.
3.2 Correlation Analyses
Now we present analyses involving correlation among different categories and tasks.
First, we compute the Pearson correlation coefficient among all pairs of categories and tasks in LiveBench (see Figure 2).
We find that unsurprisingly, math, coding, and reasoning all correlate with one another.
Interestingly, language correlates fairly well with data analysis, likely due to both categories including tasks that require the LLM to output a large part of the prompt that is modified in a specific way (e.g., by fixing typos or changing the table format).
Surprisingly, instruction following correlates relatively weakly with all other categories.
Among tasks, we see that math comp correlates the highest with the average LiveBench performance, suggesting that this task is the greatest indicator of overall model performance.
This is likely due to these being high-quality, diverse mathematical reasoning questions (which we modified to reduce contamination).

polymarket-3572142.text:
There are no ties in the rank column: each model is assigned a unique rank.
Therefore, two models are tied if their rank spreads overlap.
The raw ranking is the current best estimate of the true underlying ranking.

Today, we are announcing an update to our ranking methodology that makes our rankings both more interpretable and more accurate in how they reflect statistical uncertainty.
We are grateful to our community members for helpful suggestions that have led to this decision.
Alongside each model score, we are now reporting the raw rank and the rank spread for the respective model.
The raw rank is simply the rank of the model's Arena score.
There are no ties in the rank column: each model is assigned a unique rank.
Models in the leaderboard are sorted based on the raw rank.
Ties are reflected in the rank spread, which is an interval whose lower and upper endpoints correspond to the best and worst rank a model could have, based on all models' confidence intervals (CIs).
The scores and confidence intervals remain unchanged.
Formally, the best rank a model M can have is 1 + #{models whose lower CI endpoint is greater than model M's upper CI endpoint} .
Analogously, the worst rank a model M can have is 1 + #{models whose upper CI endpoint is greater than model M's lower CI endpoint} .
(The "1+" ensures that ranks cannot be zero; the best possible rank is one.)
Intuitively, one can interpret the rank spread as follows.
Suppose the true Arena score of model M is equal to the highest value included in its score's CI, and suppose that the true scores of all other models are the lowest values included in their respective CIs.
This "optimistic" rank is the lower endpoint of model M's rank spread.
The "pessimistic" rank is obtained analogously, by assuming model M's score is the lowest value included in its CI and all other models' scores are the highest values in their respective CIs.
This is the upper endpoint of model M's rank spread.
Therefore, two models are tied if their rank spreads overlap.
The raw ranking is the current best estimate of the true underlying ranking.
For example, in the screenshot above, gemini-2.5-pro , claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-thinking-32k, claude-opus-4-1-20250805-thinking-16k , and claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 are all contenders for the number one spot because their rank spread includes 1.
However, based on current data our best estimate is that gemini-2.5-pro has the highest true underlying score.
Previously, we only reported the "optimistic" rank, i.e.
the lower endpoint of the rank spread, as described above.
This methodology naturally assigned high ranks to models whose scores have high uncertainty, i.e.
large CIs (for example, new models on the leaderboard).
The new ranking method is more neutral, placing equal emphasis on the "optimistic" and the "pessimistic" ranking implied by the CIs.

Agent Arena Signal Definitions
Last Updated: October 12, 2026
Agent Arena ranks models on their agentic capabilities using signals drawn directly from the real work our global community of users completes on Arena - not synthetic benchmarks.
Each signal below is built from explicit confirmations or extracted from live traces: the turns, corrections, errors, and feedback that naturally occur when people use agents to get work done on Arena.ai.
Each is scored at the level of an individual turn or task before being aggregated into a model-level score.
The definitions on this page describe what each signal measures, what counts toward it, and how it rolls up: they're the ground truth for how a raw interaction becomes a number on the Agent Arena signal leaderboards.
Confirmed Success
We score every task by whether the user explicitly confirms the final outcome.
We prompt the user with a pop-up that asks: “Did this complete your task?” If the user clicks “yes”, the task counts towards a confirmed success.
If the user clicks “no”, it does not count as confirmed.
There is no partial credit for work that looks right but that was never actually validated by the user.

We recently deployed the agentic Max router in a live test, where it ranked #1 in Agent Arena with a score of +14.7% and a median cost of $3.27 per task over its testing period.

With our original Max and Multimodal Max releases, we explored model routing across chat-based and multimodal tasks.
This release continues our research into intelligent routing, tackling the challenge of balancing performance and cost across multi-turn, long-horizon tasks in Agent Arena.
Powered by 2.5+ million real-world Agent Arena sessions, Max routes users’ requests to the best models based on task complexity, cost and type of tasks.
By accounting for each model’s strengths and performance-cost tradeoffs, Max achieves Pareto-frontier performance across task categories.
In the last 4 months, we’ve tested over 60 different agentic models on Arena, revealing distinct trade-offs between performance and cost, as well as the strengths and weaknesses of models across chat, code, and work tasks.
Max matches each task with the model best suited to handle it, delivering a consistent, reliable experience across chat, work, and coding.
We recently deployed the agentic Max router in a live test, where it ranked #1 in Agent Arena with a score of +14.7% and a median cost of $3.27 per task over its testing period.
Max outperformed the #1 public model at the time of testing, Fable 5.1 (Max), by 0.3% at 37.5% lower cost*.
Below, we share further insights and a breakdown of Max’s routing distribution.
Max Router Breakdown
Max shifts the performance–cost Pareto frontier across code, chat, and work, with the largest gains in chat and work.
The solid lines show the frontier with Max, compared with the dotted lines for public models alone.
By routing between Fable 5.1, Astra medium and Astra max, Max delivers stronger results at a lower cost than directly selecting these models.
Max adapts its routing to each task: 67% of code sessions go to Astra (Medium), while chat favors Astra (Max) at 49% and Fable 5.1 (Max) at 42%.
Work sessions mostly split between Fable 5.1 (Max) at 49% and Astra (Medium) at 43%.
Max learns to identify potentially costly coding sessions that the less expensive Astra (Medium) is likely to solve successfully, selectively routing those sessions to maximize savings.

Install Muse Code on macOS or Linux:
curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | bash
Muse Code takes on complex software engineering tasks across large repositories: planning changes, writing code, and validating the results.
It can coordinate multiple persistent subagents for each task, solving difficult problems faster, more accurately, and with less intervention.
Muse Code
Async Background Agents
Muse Code operates with a simple agent loop plus a set of async background agents to enhance the main agent's capability.
These specialized background agents remain active throughout each session, rather than being spawned for individual tasks, helping avoid redundant information gathering.
They carry out next steps and choose when to communicate back to the main agent.
Their persistence reduces latency and the need for steering on difficult, multi-step tasks.
Runtime Design
Muse Code uses a local event log in which every model call, tool run, approval, and edit is appended.
Thi
[...]

This self-improvement loop helped Muse Spark 1.2 follow complex instructions more precisely than its predecessor.
Case Study: Kernel Optimization
We tested the model's ability to iteratively optimize GPU kernels over 1,000+ tool calls (up to 24 hours).
Leveraging Muse Code's agentic coding environment, the model writes, compiles, profiles, and progressively improves kernel performance relative to a provided baseline implementation.
We benchmarked on KDA and MLA kernels for NVIDIA Hopper GPUs.
The agent continues to achieve substantial improvements over the provided baseline implementation.
The baseline is the FLA Triton implementation of KDA.
Models were prohibited from importing third-party kernel libraries such as FLA directly; instead, they had to apply specialized kernel-optimization knowledge to implement the algorithm in Triton, rather than wrap existing implementations.
Muse Spark 1.2 paired a chunk-parallel preparation kernel with a sequential inter-chunk scan, combining standard fusion and tiling with KDA-specific optimizations such as re-centering the gated cumulative decay at the chunk midpoint.

In this post, we'll first explore Muse Spark's new capabilities and applications.

We continue to invest in areas with current performance gaps, such as long-horizon agentic systems and coding workflows.
With larger models in development, these results demonstrate that our stack is scaling effectively.
We’re also releasing Contemplating mode, which orchestrates multiple agents that reason in parallel.
This allows Muse Spark to compete with the extreme reasoning modes of frontier models such as Gemini Deep Think and GPT Pro.

Muse Spark is available now, and Contemplating mode will be rolling out gradually in meta.ai.

Real gross domestic product (GDP) edged up 0.1% in January, following 0.2% growth in December, driven by strength in goods-producing industries.
In January, goods-producing industries expanded by 0.2% for the second month in a row, as gains in mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction, construction and utilities more than offset a contraction in manufacturing.
Meanwhile, services-producing industries were essentially unchanged in January, as increases in retail trade and finance and insurance were offset by declines in wholesale trade and transportation and warehousing.

Mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction expanded by 1.2% in January, fully offsetting December's decline, led by increased activity in oil and gas extraction.

Growth of 2.8% in oil and gas extraction (except oil sands) reflected increased crude petroleum extraction in Newfoundland and Labrador and Saska

polymarket-5166965.text:
North Korea fired two submarine-launched cruise missiles on Wednesday in the Sea of Japan, the first public disclosure of a SLCM test firing in nearly three years.
Neither South Korea nor Japan have issued a release on the SLCM launches.
Japan Vice Minister of Defense Takashi Koyari said North Korea has launched at least 18 ballistic missiles and other projectiles 11 times this year, including Monday’s two launches.

North Korea fired two submarine-launched cruise missiles on Wednesday in the Sea of Japan, the first public disclosure of a SLCM test firing in nearly three years.
North Korea’s Missile Administration fired two types of submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles, state media Korean Central News Agency reported on Thursday.
North Korea uses the term “strategic” to describe nuclear weapons capability.
“The test-fire aimed to examine the current mobilized posture of the underwater combat systems and contributed to getting the Navy skilled in performing its strategic missions and showcasing high reliability, trustworthiness and ability of the war deterrents of the [Democratic People’s Republic of Korea],” reads the KCNA report.
North Korea’s last public disclosure of SLCM firings was in January of 2024 in which two Pulhwasal-3-31 were launched, USNI News reported at the time.
Imagery of Wednesday’s firing shows one SLCM launched vertically from underwater while another was launched from underwater at a 45-degree angle common to torpedo-launched SLCMs.
The photos released by KCNA also show the SLCMs in flight.
The state media did not disclose whether the SLCMs were fired from a submarine or underwater launch platform but included a photo of missile submarine Hero Kim Kun Ok (841) underway on the surface.
Hero Kim Kun Ok, which was commissioned in September of 2023, is the only Sinpo-C-class submarine constructed and commissioned.
North Korea, in March of 2025, showed photos of a nuclear powered ballistic missile submarine under construction.
Wednesday’s firing was overseen by General Kim Jong Sik, member of the Central Military Commission of the Workers’ Party of Korea and first vice department director of the WPK Central Committee, General Jang Chang Ha, general director of the Missile Administration and underwater weapon system engineers of the Korean People’s Army Navy (KPAN).
Neither South Korea nor Japan have issued a release on the SLCM launches.
South Korea’s Yonhap News Agency reported Joint Chiefs of Staff spokesperson Capt.
Jang Do-young said during a press briefing that South Korea’s military had tracked the SLCMs but declined to provide details.
Japan’s Ministry of Defense typically reports on missile launches that come close to Japan’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
The SLCM firings followed launches of at least two ballistic missiles on Monday.
KCNA reported Tuesday that the Missile Administration test-fired a tactical ballistic missile on Monday to confirm the success in the research for the technical upgrading of an important core element and that the test-firing is part of the regular activities of the Missile Administration and its affiliated research institutes.
“The Missile Administration announced that the technical upgrading of the core element is a big success heralding an important change in improving the performance and sophistication of all offensive weapon systems,” reads the KCNA report.
A KCNA photo shows a missile being launched from a Transporter Erector Launcher (TEL).
North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles towards the Sea of Japan from the Pyongyang area at 9:20 a.m.
local time Monday, according to Japan’s Joint Staff Office.
One of the missiles flew for more than 900 kilometers – around 560 miles, the JSO said.
The first missile reached a maximum altitude of about 13 miles, and flew for about 137 miles, according to Japan’s Ministry of Defense.
The second missile was launched at 9:36 a.m.
local time, and reached a maximum altitude of about 44 miles and flew for more than 566 miles.
In a press conference on Monday, Japan Vice Minister of Defense Takashi Koyari said North Korea has launched at least 18 ballistic missiles and other projectiles 11 times this year, including Monday’s two launches.
“The series of actions by North Korea, including the repeated launches of ballistic missiles, threaten the peace and security of Japan, the region and the international community.
Furthermore, such ballistic missile launches violate relevant Security Council resolutions and are a serious issue concerning the safety of the Japanese people.
In response to this launch, Japan has lodged a strong protest and condemned North Korea through its embassy in Beijing,” said Koyari, according to a transcript.
U.S Pacific Command said it was aware of Monday’s launches in a statement.
“Based on current assessments, this event does not pose an immediate threat to U.S.
personnel or territory, or to our allies.
The United States remains committed to the defense of the U.S.
homeland and our allies in the region,” reads the statement.

3 missile launch, North Korea claimed a flight of approximately 1,000 kilometers, while South Korea assessed more than 700 kilometers and Japan estimated about 680 kilometers.
Heavier warheads, maneuvering weapons, sea-based launches pose greater threats
North Korea is displaying an increasingly diverse missile arsenal this year, firing from different platforms — on land, aboard warships and, according to Pyongyang, underwater from a submarine — while testing weapons designed to carry heavier warheads, maneuver to evade interception and inflict damage over wider areas.
The frequency of missile tests has also increased, with 16 ballistic missile launches recorded through Oct.
12, which exceeds the six recorded in all of 2025 and 12 in 2024.
But what's more threatening than the frequency of ballistic missiles is diversification, with cruise missile tests added on seven occasions through Oct.
14, involving land-based launchers, destroyers and, purportedly, a submarine.
The expanding arsenal gives North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s military more options to approach targets from different directions and coordinate strikes, placing greater demands on South Korean and U.S.
defenses even as questions remain over Pyongyang's technological claims.
Widening range of weapons
This year's ballistic launches began near Pyongyang on Jan.
4 with suspected Hwasong-11 Ma hypersonic missiles.
North Korea then fired large-caliber rockets on Jan.
27 and 600-millimeter super-large rockets, known as KN-25, from Sunan on March 14.
Testing intensified in April — a suspected ballistic missile’s track disappeared shortly after launch on April 7, followed by two separate firings the next day, including what the North claimed was a Hwasong-11 Ga, or KN-23, cluster-warhead test.
Hwasong-11 Ra missiles were then fired on April 19.
North Korea went on to test close-range ballistic missiles on May 26 and tactical ballistic missiles with special-purpose warheads on June 25.
August brought further firings of ballistic missiles on Aug.
6 and 12, followed by suspected KN-25 rockets on Aug.
20.
Ballistic missiles also featured in a combined exercise on Sept.
12, before a claimed Hwasong-11 Ma-1 hypersonic test on Sept.
20.
The sequence continued with a claimed hypersonic intermediate-range missile launch on Oct.
3 and launches of different ballistic missile types on Oct.
12.
Separately, the destroyer Choe Hyon fired strategic cruise missiles on March 4 and 10.
A mobile short-range anti-aircraft missile system was tested during the April 6–8 weapons-testing series, followed by strategic cruise and anti-ship missile launches from Choe Hyon on April 12.
Tactical cruise missiles with claimed artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted guidance were tested alongside guided artillery rockets on May 26.
The destroyer Kang Kon tested a strategic cruise missile on July 3, while tactical cruise missiles joined rockets and attack drones in the Sept.
12 exercise.
On Oct.
14, Pyongyang tested two cruise missile types purportedly launched from a submarine.
The precise underwater launch platform remain unconfirmed.
Greater destructive potential
Asked how much North Korea’s missiles have advanced and how serious a threat they pose, experts said combat data from Russia’s war against Ukraine has helped Pyongyang improve their accuracy and ability to pinpoint targets in South Korea.
North Korea has deployed troops to fight alongside Russian forces and also supplied ballistic missiles.
“North Korea has significantly improved their accuracy using data obtained from the war in Ukraine.
This year’s launches can be seen as drawing on those accumulated findings,” said Yang Uk, a research fellow at the Asan Institute for Policy Studies.
“Years of development have made the Pyongyang’s missiles more reliable, with recent efforts focused on hitting targets more precisely,” he added.

Crypto rules finalized, Bitcoin retreats, Solana upgrades | Weekly recap
In this week’s edition of the weekly recap, US regulators finalized stablecoin rules under the GENIUS Act, Bitcoin lost ground after a sharp reversal in ETF flows, and Solana activated Alpenglow.
Corporate Bitcoin financing, institutional custody deals, and Ethereum’s postponed testnet upgrade also shaped crypto.news coverage for Oct.
18–24.
- Jan.
18, 2027, is the effective date for the OCC’s final GENIUS Act stablecoin rules.
- $635.49 million left US spot Bitcoin ETFs on Oct.
22, ending three consecutive inflow sessions.
- Solana activated Alpenglow on Oct.
21, targeting roughly 150-millisecond finality with its new consensus system.
- Strategy increased its Bitcoin holdings to 848,517 BTC and expanded its securities buyback authorization.
- Strive closed a $630 million preferred stock offering carrying a fixed 15% annual dividend rate.
GENIUS Act rules set January start date
- The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency finalized stablecoin regulations on Oct.
21, establishing standards for reserve assets, redemptions, risk management, custody and issuer supervision.
The rules take effect Jan.
18, 2027, and cover issuers and related activities under the agency’s jurisdiction.
- Existing issuers with substantially complete applications pending by the deadline may seek temporary compliance waivers while their submissions undergo review.
Anti-money laundering and sanctions provisions remain subject to a separate rulemaking with the Treasury Department.
The framework also addresses foreign issuers and transitions from state to federal oversight.
Bitcoin ETF withdrawals interrupt the recovery
- US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $635.49 million in net outflows on Oct.
22, reversing three consecutive sessions that brought in approximately $1.08 billion.
SoSoValue’s figures showed the largest daily withdrawal since June 25, with October’s cumulative flows turning negative by about $174.5 million.
- Bitcoin traded near $81,450 in crypto.news’ Oct.
23 market report after failing to sustain its recovery toward $85,000.
The retreat returned attention to the $80,000 area.
CoinGlass separately recorded roughly $406 million in liquidations across the broader cryptocurrency market over 24 hours, rather than Bitcoin alone.
Solana activates Alpenglow consensus
- Solana Foundation’s activation record confirmed Alpenglow’s deployment on mainnet during epoch 1064 on Oct.
21.
The Votor consensus system targets roughly 150-millisecond finality, compared with 12.8 seconds under TowerBFT.
Transaction execution, program behavior, and fee mechanics remain unchanged.
- Alpenglow consensus began at slot 459,653,000 after a genesis block received certification from 446 of 654 validators.
Rotor, the proposed data-distribution component, remains reserved for a later release.
Solana also promoted Quantumglow research, but the proposed post-quantum adaptation has no announced deployment date and is separate from the completed consensus migration.
Strategy adds Bitcoin and expands buybacks
- Strategy acquired another 267 Bitcoin, bringing its holdings to 848,517 BTC as of Oct.
18.

Bitcoin nears $81,000 ahead of Fed decision as ZEC jumps 8%
Majors outpaced bitcoin across the board as tech stocks extended a climb.
- Bitcoin rose nearly 2% to just under $81,000 ahead of the Federal Reserve’s rate decision, while major cryptocurrencies broadly advanced.
- Galaxy said Bitcoin’s bear market likely ended in June and that the cryptocurrency has entered an accumulation phase that historically preceded rallies.
- Traders are watching for signals of a December rate increase, while a daily Bitcoin close above $82,500 could indicate that the recovery is gaining momentum.
Bitcoin climbed nearly 2% to just under $81,000 as of Wednesday Asian morning hours, clawing back the weekend’s slip to nearly $79,000 as traders braced for the Federal Reserve’s rate decision later in the day.
ZEC led the majors, jumping 8% to about $1,320 and putting it back above $1,300 after Monday’s selloff.
HYPE added nearly 5% to about $81.
XRP and DOGE rose roughly 3%, while ether gained 2% to just above $2,350 and SOL climbed about 2% to $102.
BNB rose 1%, and TRX lagged with a gain of less than 1%, according to CoinDesk data.
The bounce came a day after Galaxy told investors that now is the time to accumulate bitcoin.
“We think the bear market ended in June and that bitcoin is in the accumulation phase that has preceded every prior advance,” Alex Thorn, head of firmwide research at Galaxy, said in the note.
Thorn said the bottom likely came in June, when bitcoin traded under $58,000.
He pointed to bitcoin’s move back above its 50-week moving average — the average of its last 50 weekly closes, which traders use to judge the longer-term trend — along with lighter selling pressure and rising U.S.
debt.
That’s a confident call for a market that has struggled to hold $80,000.
Traders will now be listening to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference for any hint of a December rate hike.
A hike would make borrowing more expensive and tends to pull money out of riskier assets like crypto.

Republican incumbent Joe Lombardo is seeking a second term.

Background
[edit]
Nevada is considered to be a purple to slightly blue state at the federal and state levels, with neither party having control of all three branches of government.
Apart from the governor, Nevada's lieutenant governor and state controller are Republicans.
Nevada's attorney general, treasurer, and state secretary of state are Democrats.[citation needed] Donald Trump won the state in 2024, becoming the first Republican presidential nominee to win the state since 2004.[2]
The Nevada Legislature is controlled by members of the Democratic Party, with a majority in both the state assembly and senate.
The lieutenant governor, a Republican, serves as the president of the state senate but only votes in the case of a tie.
At the federal level, both United States Senators and three out of four members of the United States House of Representatives from Nevada are Democrats.[3][4]

The governor of Nevada is the head of government of the U.S.
state of Nevada.[2] The governor is the head of the executive branch of the Nevada state government.
The governor is also the commander-in-chief of the state's military forces.[3] The governor has a duty to enforce state laws[4] and the power to either approve or veto bills passed by the Nevada Legislature,[5] to convene the legislature at any time,[6] as well as, except in cases of treason or impeachment, to grant pardons and reprieves.[7]
The governor of Nevada serves a four-year term.[8] An amendment in 1970 limits them to two terms, even if they are non-consecutive.[9] The lieutenant governor of Nevada is officially not elected on the same ticket as the governor.
Should there be a vacancy in the office of governor, the powers devolve onto the lieutenant governor.
The current governor is Republican Joe Lombardo, who took office on January 2, 2023.

Territory of Nevada
[edit]
Nevada Territory was formed on March 2, 1861, from Utah Territory.[10] It had only one governor appointed by the president of the United States before it became a state.
Before it was organized as a territory, a local convention in Genoa elected Isaac Roop provisional governor, taking office on December 15, 1859.[11]

Nevada was admitted to the Union on October 31, 1864.[16] There have been thirty one governors since.

Poll finds Ford leading Lombardo 49-45, Lombardo and Trump underwater
A new poll from DGA-backed A More Affordable Nevada found Attorney General Aaron Ford leading Joe Lombardo, the most vulnerable governor in the country, 49 to 45 percent in the Nevada governor’s race.
The poll shows Donald Trump’s favorability is -18, a massive vulnerability for Lombardo, who called Trump his “commanding officer” and has backed Trump’s cost-raising agenda every step of the way – including telling Nevadans to “feel a little pain” from tariffs and embracing Trump’s Iran war that has sent fuel costs to all-time highs across the state.

“Aaron Ford has clear momentum heading into the final week of this election as he runs on a clear message of lowering costs and standing up to Joe Lombardo and Donald Trump’s cost-raising agenda,” said DGA Deputy Communications Director Johanna Warshaw.
“Lombardo has stood lockstep with his ‘commanding officer’ Donald Trump and now Nevadans are feeling the pain that he promised everyday under the Lombardo-Trump economy – and that’s why he will be a one term governor.”

PAC boosting third-party NV governor candidate as 'AOC of Nevada' has GOP ties
A new campaign mailer calling Nevada nonpartisan governor candidate Danielle Ford the "AOC of Nevada" is backed by a newly formed political action committee with apparent ties to Republican political operatives.
The mailer, which features a cutout of Rep.
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) standing next to Ford against a bold red background, was paid for by the Silver State Accountability political action committee.
The PAC was created on Oct.
8 and has no online footprint — even its website listed on registration paperwork (silverstateaccountability.com) is under construction as of Tuesday.
Mike Casca, a spokesperson for Ocasio-Cortez, said Danielle Ford has never contacted or spoken to the congresswoman, who is supporting Democratic candidate and Attorney General Aaron Ford in the race.
"This mailer is a disgusting attempt to trick Nevada voters," Casca said.
"Rep.
Ocasio-Cortez is not supporting Danielle Ford for governor and any vote for Danielle is a vote for Trump's biggest fan Joe Lombardo."
Ford, a member of the state board of education and past trustee on the Clark County School District Board, has raised relatively little in her long-shot independent bid for governor, but she shares the same surname as the Democratic governor candidate, which could confuse voters.
She did not immediately respond to an email through what appears to be a press contact, a message on the social media platform X or a voicemail.
The PAC boosting her is known as a "shadow PAC" because its registrants exploited a loophole in state law by setting it up after Sept.
30, missing Nevada's campaign finance reporting deadline and avoiding donor reporting before Election Day.
However, its registration form lists an address tied to a mailbox office rental company in the same commercial complex as Gov.
Joe Lombardo's (R) campaign office, and the registered agents appear to have ties to Republicans.
With recent polling showing the governor's race a "toss-up," boosting Danielle Ford among left-leaning voters could be an attempt to muddy the waters.
In competitive races nationwide, candidates with the same last name have confused voters and even led to a disqualification.
It's also not the first time it's happened in Nevada: In 2022, Democratic groups spent six figures boosting a "Patriot Freedom Fund" shadow PAC that bashed then-candidate Lombardo from the right.
Aaron Ford campaign spokesperson Tai Sims called Danielle Ford a "MAGA plant being propped up by Joe Lombardo's Republican allies."
Halee Dobbins, a spokesperson for Lombardo's campaign, told The Nevada Independent that the campaign had no knowledge of the PAC or mailer.
Danielle Ford and the PAC
Hope Hohnke is listed as the PAC's registered agent.
Reached by The Indy on Tuesday, Hohnke directed reporters to the PAC's chairman, Dustin McIntyre.
Hohnke lives in Oklahoma and said she was not the point person for the PAC.
She shared McIntyre's email and did not answer questions about her party registration, the PAC's purpose or ties to the Republican Party.
McIntyre did not return an email seeking comment.
He's listed as treasurer for nearly 80 PACs across the country, most with Republican ties, including as the treasurer for Save Nevada NOW, a PAC run by Assm.
Lisa Cole (R-Las Vegas), which The Nevada Independent previously reported was partially funded by a conservative dark money group.
Other PACs McIntyre has registered have sent attack mailers against Nevada Democrats in recent weeks.
Danielle Ford does not appear to have previously connected herself to Ocasio-Cortez's politics.

Our top takeaways from Nevada's new campaign finance reports
Millions of dollars poured into Nevada's congressional and statewide races from July through September, according to campaign finance reports filed Thursday, giving the final financial outlook for many candidates ahead of Election Day.
Democrats had healthy fundraising leads in all but one of the state's four congressional districts.
Attorney General Aaron Ford (D) reported more direct campaign contributions in the race for governor than Gov.
Joe Lombardo (R) for the first time this election cycle, though the incumbent outspent Ford.
Large amounts of outside dollars have also poured into the race, with the Republican Governors Association (RGA) donating $9.5 million to a Lombardo-affiliated PAC and the Democratic Governors Association contributing $7 million to a separate affiliated PAC.
Billionaire hotel mogul Robert Bigelow, a longtime Lombardo megadonor, gave $6 million to the RGA's Nevada PAC.
Those big outside spending numbers have made the governor's race the one with the highest ad spending in Nevada this election cycle, according to AdImpact.
The Democratic Governors Association-affiliated PAC, A More Affordable Nevada PAC, has led Democratic ad spending in the Nevada governor's race, with AdImpact showing it has spent or reserved more than $14.1 million on campaign ads as of Friday morning.
In comparison, AdImpact shows the Lombardo-affiliated Better Nevada PAC has spent or reserved more than $29.3 million in campaign ads.
Many of the other statewide races had Democrats ahead in fundraising from July through September, especially the races for attorney general and secretary of state.
The only other statewide race with a Republican in the lead was for state controller.
Read more to see details on the fundraising hauls — and the candidates' top donors.
You can click the links below to scroll to a specific section.
Attorney general and secretary of state
Democrats up in three of four congressional races
In the 1st Congressional District, state Sen.
Carrie Buck (R-Henderson) outraised Rep.
Dina Titus (D-NV) for the fourth quarter in a row, the only GOP challenger in the country to outraise an incumbent that often.
Titus' ability to tap into her larger war chest, however, meant she spent more than Buck and still had more cash on hand in a district where she is heavily favored.
In Northern Nevada's 2nd Congressional District, former Assembly Majority Leader Teresa Benitez-Thompson (D-Reno) had the standout fundraising quarter, bringing in more than any Democratic nominee has in the 
[...]
financial disclosure to The Nevada Independent late last month, it still has not been filed with the House clerk.
In the 3rd Congressional District, Rep.
Susie Lee (D-NV) had another strong fundraising quarter, while video game composer Marty O'Donnell (R) has deployed almost all of the money he invested early on.
Even so, Lee outspent him and had seven figures in the bank going into October.
On Friday, O'Donnell gave his campaign another quarter of a million dollars.
In the 4th Congressional District, Rep.
Steven Horsford (D-NV) once again handily outraised small-business owner Cody Whipple (R) and spent about double what his challenger did.
If the GOP nominee pulls off an upset, he previously told The Nevada Independent, it will be because of his ground game, not money.
Democrats up in governor direct campaign fundraising
Though Ford outraised Lombardo, the sitting governor dwarfed his opponent in how much he raised through affiliated political action committees and from national groups.
About 14 percent of Ford's direct fundraising came from donations of $100 or less, while those types of donations made up about 2 percent of Lombardo's direct fundraising haul.
Heading into October, Lombardo reported $2.8 million in his campaign bank account, compared with Ford's more than $1.3 million.
Direct candidate donations are limited to $10,000, and Ford and Lombardo alike reported large amounts.
Those rules don't apply to political action committees.
When looking only at PAC fundraising without donations directly from national governors groups, Lombardo reported raising more than $5.8 million, while Ford reported nearly $2.7 million.
The Lombardo-aligned Better Nevada PAC received $1.8 million from a separate Lombardo-affiliated Nevada Way PAC and $750,000 from The Revitalization Project, a Virginia-based dark money nonprofit focused on the economy and "the promotion of pro-growth policies."
The Nevada Way PAC reported receiving $1 million from Station Casinos, $250,000 from Southwest Gas, $160,000 from MGM Resorts and $150,000 from South Point Hotel and Casino, though the campaign did not include these donations in its overall fundraising total.
Both PACs made up a large share of third-quarter donations to the state Republican party, contributing more than $1.8 million combined.

The 2026 Ohio gubernatorial election will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect the governor of Ohio.
Republican entrepreneur Vivek Ramaswamy and Democratic former state health director Amy Acton are the nominees for their respective parties.
Republican incumbent governor Mike DeWine is ineligible to seek a third consecutive term.
Primary elections were held on May 5, with Ramaswamy defeating minimal opposition for the Republican nomination and Acton running unopposed for the Democratic nomination.
If elected, Ramaswamy would become the first Indian American governor of Ohio and the first Hindu governor in the United States.[a] Acton would be Ohio's first elected female[b] and first Jewish governor if elected.
The campaign has been described as "ugly" and heavily reliant on negative campaigning.
Ramaswamy has focused on Acton's background to portray her as dishonest and mentally ill, while Acton has portrayed Ramaswamy as an out-of-touch plutocrat and con artist.[1]
Democrats have not won a gubernatorial election in Ohio since 2006.
The winner of the election will be inaugurated on January 11, 2027.[2]

COLUMBUS, Ohio (WSYX) — Republican Vivek Ramaswamy holds a narrow 47% to 45% edge over Democrat Amy Acton in Ohio’s gubernatorial contest, according to a survey conducted October 16–23, 2026, by Echelon Insights for tech industry group NetChoice.
Libertarian Don Kissick drew 4%.
Because the two-point margin falls well within the survey’s 5.2 percentage point margin of error, the contest remains a statistical dead heat one week out from election day in Ohio.
Echelon Insights is an established polling firm that samples from verified voter files.
More Key Findings
- State Issue 3: 70% of Ohio voters support the proposed constitutional amendment requiring photo ID to vote, while 28% oppose it.
- Top Voter Concern: Inflation and the cost of living led voter priorities at 57%, outpacing foreign policy (24%) and healthcare costs (21%).
- Antitrust & AI: 73% of respondents favor applying the consumer welfare standard to antitrust enforcement, 86% want antitrust laws applied equally to all companies, and 70% say Congress—not individual states—should establish national AI rules.
NOTE: This survey was commissioned by an industry trade association testing public sentiment on tech.
The survey sampled 508 likely Ohio voters via online, text and panel invitations.

Ohio Gov.
Mike DeWine on Thursday called for Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican he endorsed to succeed him as governor, to stop airing an ad that features the estranged mother of Ramaswamy’s Democratic opponent, Amy Acton.
“The ad, on its face, is deeply, deeply troubling,” DeWine said at a news conference he called to address what has become a boiling controversy in the final days of a hostile race.
His comments drew a rebuke later Thursday from President Donald Trump, who chastised him on Truth Social and called the Ramaswamy spot a “very powerful Ad.”
DeWine, for his part, reaffirmed his support for Ramaswamy.
“Look, today is about the ad, but I’m not — no, I’m not changing my endorsement,” he said when reporters pressed him at the Ohio Statehouse.
“I endorse the whole ticket, as you know.
I’m a Republican.
I endorse the whole ticket.
On that ticket are some amazing people, almost all of whom I have worked with in the past.”
The Ramaswamy campaign ad, backed by a $4 million purchase of statewide airtime, features Donna Arthur, who calls her daughter a “liar” in the minutelong spot and urges Ohioans not to vote for her.
Acton has talked about having been sexually abused by her mother’s husband as a child.
Her brother, Philip Stearns, has corroborated her account, saying in a video for Acton’s campaign that their “birth mother stayed married to Amy’s rapist until he died.”
Acton has said she has not seen or spoken to her mother in nearly 50 years.
Arthur has not responded to requests for comment.
The ad did not refer to the abuse claims.
But DeWine on Thursday talked about prosecuting sexual assault cases earlier in his career in public service and said he found the ad troubling given the family history.
“When you know the rest of the story, when you know the backstory, when you know that the husband of the mom was indicted by a grand jury after hearing testimony and that he took off along with the mother ...
and that two children never saw, I guess, the mother after that — when you know that, it just to me makes it more serious,” he said.
